exercises.title: Bài 1 · How the legal system works
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Every country has a legal system, which is a set of rules that people, companies and governments must follow. The highest law is usually the constitution. Below it are statutes, which are written by the legislature, and regulations, which explain how the statutes work in practice.

Legal systems are often divided into two main types. In common law countries, such as the United Kingdom, judges follow precedent, so earlier court decisions are very important. In civil law countries, such as France, courts mainly apply written codes. Vietnam also follows a civil law tradition.

Law is divided into different areas. Criminal law deals with crimes and punishes offenders, while civil law deals with private disputes, for example between a company and its supplier. In a civil case, the plaintiff brings a claim, and the defendant must respond. A judge listens to the witnesses, examines the evidence and then gives a ruling.

content.q: The constitution is usually the highest law in a country.
content.why: Đoạn 1: 'The highest law is usually the constitution'.

content.q: In common law countries, judges follow precedent.
content.why: Đoạn 2: thẩm phán theo tiền lệ.

content.q: Criminal law deals with private disputes between companies.
content.why: Đoạn 3: luật hình sự xử lý tội phạm; tranh chấp tư thuộc luật dân sự.

content.q: In a civil case, the defendant brings the claim.
content.why: Đoạn 3: **plaintiff** (nguyên đơn) đưa ra yêu cầu, bị đơn phải phản hồi.

content.q: What are regulations?
content.why: Đoạn 1: quy định giải thích cách các đạo luật vận hành trong thực tế.
opts: Rules that explain how statutes work in practice

content.q: Which country is mentioned as a common law country?
content.why: Đoạn 2: Vương quốc Anh là nước thông luật; Pháp và Việt Nam theo dân luật.

content.q: What does a judge do in a civil case?
content.why: Đoạn 3: thẩm phán nghe nhân chứng, xem bằng chứng và đưa ra phán quyết.
opts: Brings a claim against the defendant
Examines the evidence and gives a ruling

content.q: What does criminal law do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: luật hình sự xử lý tội phạm và trừng phạt người phạm tội.
opts: Applies only in civil law countries
Deals with crimes and punishes offenders

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How a contract is formed
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties. For a contract to be valid, four elements are usually required. First, an offer is made by one party. Second, the offer is accepted by the other party. Third, something of value, called consideration, is exchanged. Finally, both parties must intend to create legal relations.

Most commercial contracts are written. The terms and conditions are negotiated, and then the document is drafted by lawyers and signed by both parties. Important clauses include payment, delivery, confidentiality and governing law. If a contract is changed, an amendment must be signed.

When a party fails to perform, a breach of contract has occurred. The other party can ask the court to order damages, which are paid as compensation. However, a party is not responsible if performance is prevented by force majeure, such as a flood or a war.

content.q: A contract is a legally binding agreement.
content.why: Đoạn 1: hợp đồng là thỏa thuận ràng buộc về mặt pháp lý.

content.q: Consideration means that something of value is exchanged.
content.why: Đoạn 1: consideration là thứ có giá trị được trao đổi.

content.q: A contract can be changed without any written document.
content.why: Đoạn 2: khi hợp đồng thay đổi, phải ký một văn bản sửa đổi (amendment).

content.q: A party is always responsible for a breach, even in the case of force majeure.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bên vi phạm không chịu trách nhiệm nếu bị cản trở bởi bất khả kháng.

content.q: Who usually drafts commercial contracts?
content.why: Đoạn 2: văn bản được luật sư soạn thảo.

content.q: Which clauses are important?
content.why: Đoạn 2: thanh toán, giao hàng, bảo mật và luật điều chỉnh.
opts: Payment, delivery, confidentiality and governing law

content.q: What can the other party ask the court to do after a breach?
content.why: Đoạn 3: yêu cầu tòa án buộc bồi thường thiệt hại.

content.q: Which event can prevent performance without a breach?
content.why: Đoạn 3: lũ lụt hoặc chiến tranh là trường hợp bất khả kháng.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Choosing a type of business
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
When entrepreneurs start a business, they have to choose a legal form. The simplest option is a sole proprietorship. It is cheaper and easier to set up than a company, but the owner is personally responsible for all debts. A partnership is similar, although the risks and profits are shared by two or more partners.

A limited liability company (LLC) is usually safer for the owners because their liability is limited to the capital they have invested. It is more complicated to set up, and it must follow stricter rules on registration and accounting. A joint-stock company is the best choice for raising large amounts of capital, because it can sell shares to many investors. The shareholders elect a board of directors, and the more shares a person owns, the more votes he or she has.

If a company grows, it may create subsidiaries or join another company in a merger.

content.q: A sole proprietorship is easier to set up than a company.
content.why: Đoạn 1: doanh nghiệp tư nhân rẻ và dễ thành lập hơn.

content.q: The owner of a sole proprietorship has limited liability.
content.why: Đoạn 1: chủ sở hữu chịu trách nhiệm cá nhân cho mọi khoản nợ.

content.q: A joint-stock company can sell shares to many investors.
content.why: Đoạn 2: công ty cổ phần có thể bán cổ phần cho nhiều nhà đầu tư.

content.q: A shareholder with fewer shares has more votes.
content.why: Đoạn 2: càng sở hữu nhiều cổ phần thì càng có nhiều phiếu bầu.

content.q: Why is an LLC usually safer for owners?
content.why: Đoạn 2: trách nhiệm chỉ giới hạn trong số vốn đã góp.
opts: Their liability is limited to the capital they have invested
It is cheaper to set up

content.q: Which type of business is best for raising large capital?
content.why: Đoạn 2: công ty cổ phần có thể bán cổ phần cho nhiều nhà đầu tư.

content.q: Who elects the board of directors?
content.why: Đoạn 2: cổ đông bầu hội đồng quản trị.

content.q: What may a growing company create?
content.why: Đoạn cuối: công ty có thể lập công ty con hoặc sáp nhập.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · A first international sale
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Linh's company wants to sell furniture to a buyer in Germany. First, the two parties must sign a sales contract. The contract has to state the price, the quantity, the delivery date and the payment terms. The buyer doesn't have to pay the full price in advance, but the seller may ask for a deposit of 30 percent.

For payment, the buyer can open a letter of credit at its bank. The bank must pay the seller if the seller presents the correct documents. The seller should check every document carefully, because even a small mistake can delay payment.

The seller also has to follow export rules and must not ship goods to a country under an embargo. In addition, the company should check whether a free trade agreement applies, because it can reduce the tariff. After delivery, the title to the goods passes to the buyer.

content.q: The sales contract has to state the price and the delivery date.
content.why: Đoạn 1: hợp đồng phải nêu giá, số lượng, ngày giao hàng và điều khoản thanh toán.

content.q: The buyer must pay the full price in advance.
content.why: Đoạn 1: người mua **không cần** trả toàn bộ trước (don't have to).

content.q: The seller should check the documents carefully for a letter of credit.
content.why: Đoạn 2: một sai sót nhỏ cũng có thể làm chậm thanh toán.

content.q: A company may ship goods to a country under an embargo.
content.why: Đoạn 3: 'must not ship goods to a country under an embargo'.

content.q: How much deposit may the seller ask for?
content.why: Đoạn 1: bên bán có thể yêu cầu đặt cọc 30%.

content.q: When must the bank pay the seller under a letter of credit?
content.why: Đoạn 2: ngân hàng phải trả tiền khi người bán xuất trình đúng chứng từ.
opts: When the buyer signs the invoice
When the seller presents the correct documents
When the goods arrive at the port

content.q: Why can a free trade agreement be useful?
content.why: Đoạn 3: FTA có thể giảm thuế quan.

content.q: What happens after delivery?
content.why: Đoạn 3: sau khi giao hàng, quyền sở hữu hàng hóa chuyển cho bên mua.
opts: The title to the goods passes to the buyer

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Resolving a commercial dispute
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
When a commercial dispute arises, the parties have several options. The first step is usually negotiation. If the parties reach an amicable solution, they save time and money. If negotiation fails, they may try mediation, in which a neutral mediator helps them find a compromise. The mediator cannot force a decision.

If the contract has an arbitration clause, the dispute will be sent to an arbitral tribunal. Arbitration is often faster and more confidential than litigation, and the award is final. Many companies prefer arbitration for international contracts, because an arbitral award can be enforced in many countries.

If there is no arbitration clause, a party can sue in court. However, litigation can be slow and expensive. If a company lost the case, it would usually have to pay the winner's legal fees and court costs. For this reason, many lawyers say that a good settlement is better than a long trial.

content.q: Negotiation is usually the first step in resolving a dispute.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bước đầu tiên thường là đàm phán.

content.q: A mediator can force the parties to accept a decision.
content.why: Đoạn 1: hòa giải viên không thể ép đưa ra quyết định.

content.q: Arbitration is often more confidential than litigation.
content.why: Đoạn 2: trọng tài thường nhanh và bảo mật hơn kiện tụng.

content.q: Litigation is always faster than arbitration.
content.why: Đoạn 2–3: kiện tụng có thể chậm và tốn kém; trọng tài thường nhanh hơn.

content.q: What happens if the parties reach an amicable solution?
content.why: Đoạn 1: họ tiết kiệm thời gian và tiền bạc.

content.q: Where will the dispute go if the contract has an arbitration clause?
content.why: Đoạn 2: tranh chấp được chuyển đến hội đồng trọng tài.

content.q: Why do many companies prefer arbitration for international contracts?
content.why: Đoạn 2: phán quyết trọng tài có thể được thi hành ở nhiều quốc gia.
opts: An arbitral award can be enforced in many countries

content.q: What would a losing company usually have to pay?
content.why: Đoạn 3: bên thua thường phải trả phí luật sư và án phí của bên thắng.
opts: The winner's legal fees and court costs

exercises.title: Bài 1 · A trademark case
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
In 2021, a small Vietnamese coffee company registered its logo as a trademark. Two years later, a larger company started to sell coffee with a very similar logo. The owner of the small company felt that this was trademark infringement, so he asked a lawyer for advice.

The lawyer sent a warning letter and then filed a lawsuit. Since then, the court has held two hearings. The large company has argued that the two logos are different, but the judge has already seen enough evidence of confusion. Last month, the court issued an injunction, which ordered the larger company to stop selling the product.

This case shows why intellectual property matters. Since the case began, many small businesses have registered their trademarks, and several have introduced compliance programmes to avoid problems. A good company always carries out due diligence before it chooses a brand name.

content.q: The small company registered its logo as a trademark in 2021.
content.why: Đoạn 1: năm 2021 công ty nhỏ đăng ký logo làm nhãn hiệu.

content.q: The larger company started to sell coffee before the small company registered its logo.
content.why: Đoạn 1: công ty lớn bắt đầu bán **hai năm sau** khi nhãn hiệu được đăng ký.

content.q: The court has held two hearings since the case began.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'Since then, the court has held two hearings'.

content.q: The court refused to issue an injunction.
content.why: Đoạn 2: tòa đã ban hành lệnh buộc công ty lớn ngừng bán sản phẩm.

content.q: What did the owner do after he found the similar logo?
content.why: Đoạn 1: ông nhờ luật sư tư vấn.
opts: He asked a lawyer for advice

content.q: What did the large company argue?
content.why: Đoạn 2: công ty lớn lập luận hai logo khác nhau.
opts: That the two logos are different
That the small company had infringed

content.q: What did the injunction order?
content.why: Đoạn 2: lệnh buộc công ty lớn ngừng bán sản phẩm.
opts: The larger company to stop selling the product
The small company to pay royalties

content.q: What has happened since the case began?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nhiều doanh nghiệp nhỏ đã đăng ký nhãn hiệu.
opts: Many small businesses have registered their trademarks
The court has closed all coffee companies
